title: Jesse Minter Announces Joe Fagnano As Starting Quarterback vs. Jaguars
headline: Joe Fagnano starts at QB Thursday vs. Jacksonville; Lamar Jackson's availability is still undetermined and Tyler Huntley is out, possibly heading to IR.
summary: Minter confirmed that Joe Fagnano will start at quarterback Thursday night against Jacksonville, calling it an opportunity and saying the team is excited to play in front of its fans. He praised Fagnano for taking advantage of his chances since training camp, noting that he got few reps in OTAs because of the quarterback numbers but gained more work after an injury at the position about ten days before the first preseason game. Minter described Fagnano as calm and composed, said the offense ran smoothly with him in the preseason, and said the familiarity with terminology and calls from past stints should help him operate on a short week. He said the other leaders have responded well and laid out the formula for winning: run the ball, protect and play well around Fagnano, and make game-changing plays on defense and special teams. On Jacksonville, Minter pointed to their physical run and pass game, strong backs who break tackles, skill players like Parker Washington, and Trevor Lawrence and Liam Coen's offense. He said the team would need to stop the run and make plays on defense. Asked about Lamar Jackson's status for this week, Minter said the team would know the final answer at some point before Thursday. He said Tyler Huntley is out and could be placed on IR, with more details expected soon.

injuries.detail: Out for the Jaguars game; Minter said he is potentially an IR candidate, with the full picture expected within a day or so.
Asked whether he would have to play this week, Minter said the final determination would come at some point before Thursday. Nothing confirmed.

signals.note: Confirmed starter for a primetime game; he is a streaming QB option, though a backup-level passing ceiling is likely given the run-focused game plan.

Minter referenced a recent roster addition of Kedon Slovis to the quarterback mix, plus other moves such as a practice squad addition and a quarterback workout, without details.

title: Jesse Minter Discusses Quarterback Injuries
headline: Lamar Jackson is injured with no timetable yet (update possibly this week); Tyler Huntley probably won't play Thursday, and Joe Fagnano is expected to have a chance to start vs. Jacksonville despite nagging issues.
summary: Minter said the Ravens are about 70 hours from a Thursday night home game against a good Jaguars team. Joe Fagnano is dealing with a couple of issues but is expected to have a chance to play, and Minter said the starter will be settled over the next day or two. Tyler Huntley is still working through an injury and probably won't play this week, though Minter left the long-term outlook open. Minter would not say what Lamar Jackson's injury is, whether he has had surgery (he hasn't), or how long he'll be out, only that a clearer timeline may come this week. He said the team has to lean on every phase, including defense and special teams, and may need a different style of offense without Lamar. He acknowledged the offensive line lacks continuity and needs to improve in pass protection and the run game, while calling the quarterback injuries somewhat fluky. He backed Roger Rosengarten, who felt responsible for Lamar's injury. On defense, he cited explosive pass plays and fourth-down stops as the issues, but said he liked the team's fight. Kicker Tyler Loop is dealing with a small injury that grew and may go on IR, so Moody will kick Thursday.

title: Dave Canales: 'There’s an urgency about the group right now'
headline: Bryce Young looked fully mobile and ready in practice; Damien Lewis is day-to-day with a knee issue, while Brady Christensen returned to practice and the Panthers' defense is reorganizing under Todd Wash.
summary: Canales opened by noting that Brady Christensen was back at practice, and he said Bryce Young looked great moving around and is ready to go. The offensive playbook is fully open, with no changes to the play calls because of Young's mobility. Damien Lewis (knee) did not practice but moved around some earlier, and Canales called him day-to-day. Torricelli Simpkins and Corey Bullock were on the field at guard, but Canales would only say they are taking it one practice at a time. On defense, a coordinator was moved out, the staff was reshuffled so Todd Wash can focus on coordinating, and Canales declined to discuss scheme beyond saying the team is built as a 3-4 and will play its best 11. His top defensive priority for Sunday is stopping the run. He was noncommittal on the trade deadline and cap space, deferring to the front office, though the team is open to options. He praised Denver's discipline, takeaways and close-game finishing, and noted Bo Nix protects the ball and Sean Payton builds the offense around his playmakers.

title: Ben Johnson: 'These guys earned this victory ... I couldn't be more proud of them' | Press Conference
headline: Bears beat Seattle 34-17 behind a patient run game (Swift 27 carries, 3 TDs) and a more trusted Caleb Williams; Grady Jarrett (groin) and Kentavius Street (knee) are uncertain on a short week.
summary: Johnson opened by naming two injuries from the game: Grady Jarrett with a groin issue and Kentavius Street with a knee issue. He said the team will see how they are on a short week. He praised Seattle as a top defense with a top-five special teams unit, and said the physical approach showed up on a 17-play, 80-yard opening drive. The plan was to stay patient with the run game, turning small gains into bigger ones against a strong front. He credited Garrett Bradbury for communication, said D'Andre Swift's 27 carries and three touchdowns were all hard-earned yards, and said the receivers blocked well. Caleb Williams handled one of the more elaborate game plans of the year, took care of the ball, and stayed calm despite crowd noise that caused a couple of delay-of-game and false-start penalties. Johnson said Williams is clearly further along in the offense than a year ago, and noted his extra hour of work after practice with JT Baird. He also praised a newly added defender who played his first game for a share of the tackle lead and a sack, and another player who blocked a field goal and forced an interception. Both got game balls. Johnson said the team is still building, will look at areas to improve over the bye week, and is focused on going 1-0 against a hot opponent next week. He said pre-snap penalties bother him and the offense had several three-and-outs.

title: Jim Harbaugh on Justin Herbert's Performance and Continued Team Improvement
headline: Harbaugh says the Chargers will look at giving one back a steadier workload instead of a three-way rotation. Njoku's practice window is likely to open, and Herbert got a mostly positive review after the offense's touchdown drought reached 27 drives.
summary: Harbaugh spoke the day after the Week 8 loss to the Rams. He said Rodney Shelley and Donte Jackson will keep ramping up in practice and Brenen Thompson is unlikely to practice this week. Deane Leonard is still in concussion protocol, and the team will likely open David Njoku's practice window. He praised the offensive line shuffle: Joe Alt played like an elite player at left tackle and Travis Burke moved from left to right and did a good job. On Justin Herbert, he said Herbert mostly did his job well, with two throws he'd like back, and he rejected the idea that he had called Herbert's play desperate. He acknowledged the nine-quarter, 27-drive touchdown drought and the weak run game, and said the team will probably try giving one back a consistent rhythm instead of rotating three 'very good' backs. On the trade deadline he deflected to the Texans game but said he wants Khalil Mack here and called him a pillar of the team. He praised the defense, singling out Tarheeb Still (first interception of the season) and Isas Waxter, and said the unit is playing well without Derwin James.

title: HC Jeff Hafley - Nov 2 | Press Conference
headline: Kadyn Proctor remains in concussion protocol; Malik Willis played well but not cleanly. Rookie WRs Kevin Coleman Jr., Chris Bell and Caleb Douglas are producing, and Jarrett Kingston may start again at guard.
summary: Hafley said Kadyn Proctor is still in the concussion protocol and progressing through the steps. He liked Malik Willis's tape, citing clean decisions, big throws, a touchdown pass and third-down conversions, while noting room to improve with his throws, legs and decision-making. Rookie guard Jarrett Kingston started slowly but finished well in his first start, and Hafley said he would be ready if he goes again next week. Jonah Savaiinaea had the same slow-start, strong-finish pattern. Hafley praised the rookie receivers (Coleman, Bell, Douglas) for competing against New England's good secondary and gave Malik Washington credit too. Jaylen Wright has been a reliable, near-breakaway kick returner, and Hafley said he has not lost confidence in him as a running back, adding that his time will come. Kaytron Allen was praised for effort on special teams, and Hafley said he could appear in the backfield this week or next. Of the injured players, one defender (Baker) has the best chance to return this week, while Seydou Traore is not expected back this week or next. Hafley also discussed the defense's improved situational play, a sack caused by a mis-run route by the receivers, and his plan to coach Ollie on penalties.

title: Head Coach Mike Macdonald Discusses The Week 8 Loss To The Bears
headline: Seahawks fell to the Bears in Week 8 and the run game is a concern with offensive line changes; RBs came out okay, Leonard Williams has a stinger, and a short week follows.
summary: Macdonald opened by crediting the Bears for winning all three phases and said Seattle got beat, with plenty of work to do on a short week. He said he had no great answer yet on the run game struggles, noting the team felt good last week but has made changes on the offensive line, and he expects improvement. Asked about the running back rotation, he declined to discuss play counts and said the flow of the game dictated how the backs were used. On Sam Darnold, he wants to keep encouraging him to use his legs and playmaking, but said the staff can design and coach better so throws come on time, and that poor early-down efficiency makes things tough. He blamed special teams issues on kickoff return timing not syncing with blocks given the new kickoff timing. On the lack of production beyond Jaxon Smith-Njigba, he said the offense didn't execute and that if they run the ball and are dialed in, the ball will be distributed more evenly. On injuries, the running backs came out okay, Leonard Williams had a stinger, and Connor O'Toole has a foot injury. He gave no real read on how Quenton Nelson played.
